data.title: Fed Needs to Implement at Least Two More Rate Increases, Dallas Fed's Logan Says — Update
data.description:
By Jessica Coacci

The Federal Reserve needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases given the current economic outlook after the central bank voted to hold interest rates steady this week, according to Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan.

Without any monetary-policy restraint, inflation will continue to trend above target unless unexpected shocks occur, Logan said at an event in Davidson, N.C., on Friday.

"It remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the FOMC needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases," Logan said. "After that, it would make sense in my view to pause and examine economic and financial developments to determine what further action may be appropriate," she added.

There had been speculation that Logan would dissent at October's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, given her previous calls for tighter monetary policy and a previous dissent she gave in July. On Friday, she offered more explanation to why she instead supported the committee's decision to hold interest rates where they are.

Financial markets have been volatile in response to news on the technology-investment outlook and geopolitical developments, she said. In such an environment, adjusting policy more gradually can help households, businesses and market participants adapt to higher rates and reduce the risk that economic activity deteriorates more sharply than necessary, she added.

Moreover, Logan said the precise timing of each rate increase has little effect on the longer-term rates most borrowers pay as long as market participants understand the FOMC's policy plans.

In addition, skipping a meeting of rate increases doesn't change the monetary-policy destination, Logan argued.

"By making the destination clear, the FOMC can better help the economy adapt and obtain the promised benefits of a skip," she explained.

Given the current outlook, the end goal should be to make policy modestly restrictive to sustainably deliver both maximum employment and stable prices, Logan said.

Write to Jessica Coacci at jessica.coacci@wsj.com

data.title: Bank of Canada Must Rethink Further Rate Hikes Amid 'Squishy-Soft' Data — Market Talk
data.description: Days after raising its policy rate by a quarter point, the Bank of Canada faces a reality check over its outlook for accelerating growth, says David Rosenberg, head of market-strategy firm Rosenberg Research. Data covering non-farm payrolls indicate a 49,600 decline in jobs in August. Further, GDP stalled in August, and is expected to contract in September--leading to annualized growth of 1.3% in 3Q, or well below the BOC's 2% forecast. "Can the central bank really ignore the economy and this recent squishy-soft set of economic data?," says Rosenberg about pending rate hikes. He argues BOC based its rate-hike decision on "dubious surveys instead of facts on the ground," adding there is no evidence of elevated fuel prices spilling over to non-energy goods. (paul.vieira@wsj.com, @paulvieira)

data.title: AMD Stocks Drop 11% With a $13 Billion Revenue Test Approaching
data.description:
Advanced Micro Devices , the processor and AI-accelerator designer, has a bigger hurdle than winning server business: turning that growth into profit. Shares fell 11.01% to $504.05 at 12:45 p.m. ET on October 30, ahead of its November 3 earnings report. Susquehanna raised its price target from $620 to $650 and maintained Buy, pointing to data-center opportunities while flagging margin pressure from the GPU ramp. That leaves investors weighing a bigger sales opportunity against the cost of delivering it.

The numbers give that debate a clear test. AMD's August outlook called for September-quarter revenue of $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million, with adjusted gross margin near 56%. The revenue midpoint implies roughly 12.7% growth from the June quarter's $11.536 billion. More revenue could strengthen the AI story, but holding margins while expanding GPU deliveries would provide firmer evidence that the opportunity is translating into profitable growth.

GuruFocus' snapshot captures the tension: an 82/100 GF Score, strong growth and financial-strength readings, but a weak GF Value reading. At 129.34 times earnings and 12.24 times book value, the valuation appears to leave limited room for disappointment even after the sharp decline. Susquehanna's roughly 4.8% target increase adds optimism; November's results must supply the evidence. Revenue delivery, gross margin and the next outlook could determine whether AMD's expanding data-center business can support those expectations.

data.title: EU wheat ends higher, posts second weekly loss
data.description:
European wheat rose for a second consecutive session on Friday but lost 2.5% on the week, after hitting a three-month low on Wednesday on prospects of higher Russian wheat supplies.

Benchmark December milling wheat on Paris-based Euronext, ended 0.3% higher at €227.75 ($255) a metric ton.

Chicago wheat was also 0.3% higher, supported by strong demand for US grain and reports that China could buy from the United States.

"The wheat move is encouraging, but it remains to be seen whether one strong sales week and a Chinese inquiry are enough to call a bottom," CM Navigator analysts said.

"Russian export flows are rebuilding through alternative routes, while Argentine new-crop wheat is getting cheaper," they added.

Traders have also been keeping a close eye on both geopolitical tensions and investor positioning ahead of next week's US mid-term elections, said market analysts.

In its latest monthly estimates the European Commission on Friday lowered its 2026/27 EU maize production forecast to 47.0 million metric tons, from 48.3 million in September.

It also cut its soft wheat output estimate to 123.7 million tons, from 124.2 million seen in September and reduced its ending stock projection to 10.6 million tons, from 11.4 million.

Its projection of 2026/27 EU soft wheat exports was left unchanged at 29.0 million tons.

data.title: Polish president turns back from Senegal trip as top court chief suspended
data.description:
Polish President Karol Nawrocki turned back his plane en route to Senegal on Friday after police entered the premises of Poland's top court and its president was suspended.

"At a moment like this, the President must be in Poland. I am cutting short my flight to Senegal. I am returning," he said on X.

Police said officers entered the premises of the Constitutional Tribunal after incidents outside the court, including the throwing of dangerous objects at police.

The tribunal said on its website that the court's president, Bogdan Swieczkowski, had been suspended on Friday.

A long-running political dispute over the Constitutional Tribunal has effectively paralysed the institution.

Earlier this year, Nawrocki, an ally of Poland's former nationalist government, refused to swear in three of six judges nominated by parliament, while Swieczkowski declined to allow judges elected by the current parliamentary majority to assume their duties.

data.title: Vijay Kedia's portfolio stock under Rs.150: This textile stock adds Rs.3.7 crore to his wealth since IPO; Do you own?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 30 -- Vijay Kedia's portfolio stock under Rs.150: Ace investor Vijay Kedia portfolio stock, Ashutosh Fibre Limited, has delivered 6.26% return over the past week. He owns 10.35 lakh shares in the textile stock, which is equivalent to 4.73% stake in the firm.

Kedia held shares in Ashutosh Fibre before its initial public offering, and the textile stock's rally has significantly boosted the value of the ace investor's holding.

Ashutosh Fibre's SME IPO was listed on exchanges in September this year. The IPO's upper price band was fixed at Rs.92 per share. Considering Ashutosh Fibre's October 30 closing price, the stock has generated a notional gain of Rs.3.74 crore.

Investors must note that Vijay Kedia held stakes in Ashutosh Fibre Limited even before the IPO launch, hence his original acquisition cost and profit from the stock may be different. The calculation only reflects his wealth appreciation from Ashutosh Fibre against the IPO issue price.

The SME textile stock closed 1.54% lower at Rs.128.10 per share on NSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.280.22 crore. Its share price value has surged 6.26% over the past one week. But the textile stock has declined 15.96% in one month.

The Gujarat-headquartered, Ashutosh Fibre manufactures technical and synthetic yarns which is used in industrial and specialized applications. Its products include yarns which are used in filtration materials, flame-retardant workwear, personal protective equipment (PPE), automotive seat fabrics and carpets.

The company was established in 1985 and operates a manufacturing facility in Gujarat's Petlad. It produces technical and synthetic yarns for industrial and specialized applications.

data.title: Ameriprise Financial 3Q 2026: Revenue $5.19B, Net income $1.13B, EPS $12.32— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Ameriprise Financial reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $5.19 billion, up 6.1% from a year earlier, while net income rose 23.5% to $1.13 billion and diluted EPS increased 32% to $12.32.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $5.19B, compared with $4.89B in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 6.1%.
  • Net income was $1.13B, compared with $912M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 23.5%.
  • Diluted EPS was $12.32, compared with $9.33 in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 32%.

Business Highlights

  • Advice & Wealth adjusted earnings rose 16% year to date, supported by market gains, client inflows and advisor productivity. Advisory wrap assets increased 18% year over year, with nine-month net inflows of $17.8B.
  • Asset Management adjusted earnings increased 18% year to date, aided by equity markets and strong Seligman technology strategies despite net outflows.
  • Retirement & Protection adjusted earnings fell 19% year to date, reflecting assumption updates, annuity outflows and higher sales-related costs.
  • Ameriprise continues to recruit experienced advisors and expects the shift toward lower-risk products and away from variable annuity living-benefit guarantees to continue.

Original SEC Filing: AMERIPRISE FINANCIAL INC [ AMP ] - 10-Q - Oct. 30, 2026
